output.brief: The rise is not mainly a handling problem. Since 1 September, Corvane's tags printed at Harlow Bay (on the new Fennick stock) fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% before. Corvane transfer tags and Pelion tags, which Tessaly also handles, stay near 1.3–1.4%. Bags sent to manual encoding went from about 70 a day to about 470. Encode dwell rose from 7 to 33 minutes, and 91% of the encode-path bags that missed their flights reached the lateral after it closed. Bags on the automatic path are unchanged. On 14–16 October, counters that used old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12.1%. That points strongly at the tag stock, or the stock combined with printer settings. We can't yet say whether the stock is defective or just needs different printer heat settings. Don't send the breach notice or withhold the fee. Pelion's rate didn't rise on the same Tessaly crew pool. Return to Brackwater stock now; it is reversible and about five weeks are in stores. Test the Fennick stock and printer settings separately, and hold any claim against Fennick until the cause is known. A temporary extra encode workstation is a reasonable stopgap.
